title: Time zones
examples: How do time zones work around the world?
What is the difference between GMT and local time?
Why is the date line important for travel?

explain.say: The Earth takes time to spin around. It takes a full 24 hours to complete one turn.
Because the Earth spins, different places experience day and night at different times. This is what creates time zones.
We use Greenwich Mean Time or GMT as a main reference point. This is the time at the Prime Meridian.
The Earth turns 15 degrees every single hour. This helps us calculate time differences easily.
The date line is a special imaginary line on the map. It marks where the date officially changes.
Imagine you are flying from New York to London. You must adjust your watch for the time difference.

items: Arrive and adjust to London Time

faq.q: What is the difference between GMT and UTC?
faq.a: GMT stands for Greenwich Mean Time, and UTC stands for Coordinated Universal Time. For most school purposes, they are treated as the same reference time.
asks: Is UTC the same as GMT?

faq.q: Do all countries use the same time zone?
faq.a: No, countries are divided into many time zones based on their longitude. This keeps local time accurate for everyone.
asks: Why are there different times everywhere?
Does every place have its own time?

faq.q: How do I calculate the time difference between two cities?
faq.a: You can use the difference in longitude between the two places. Remember that 15 degrees equals one hour.
asks: If one place is 45 degrees away, what is the time difference?

faq.q: Why is the date line important?
faq.a: The date line helps us keep track of the calendar date as we cross the globe. It prevents us from thinking the date is wrong.
asks: What happens when you cross the date line?
Does the date change when you cross the date line?

faq.q: Is the date line exactly at 180 degrees longitude?
faq.a: The date line is located near 180 degrees longitude on the opposite side of the Earth. This is where the international date line is drawn.
asks: Where is the date line located?
What is the longitude of the date line?

facts: The Earth completes one full rotation in approximately 24 hours.
Time zones are used to keep local time accurate across different longitudes.
The Prime Meridian passes through Greenwich, England, setting GMT.
The Earth rotates 360 degrees in 24 hours, which is 15 degrees per hour.

quiz.say: If a place is 60 degrees east of GMT, what time difference should you use?
quiz.why: Since 15 degrees equals one hour, 60 degrees divided by 15 equals four hours.

wrong.0: Students might incorrectly use the 360 degree total.
wrong.2: Students might multiply 60 by 15 instead of dividing.
wrong.3: Students might confuse the degree measurement with the time difference.

quiz.say: What is the main purpose of the date line?

options.show: It marks the time zone boundary.
options.say: It marks the time zone boundary.

options.show: It marks the beginning of the day.
options.say: It marks the beginning of the day.

options.show: To mark where the calendar date changes.
options.say: To mark where the calendar date changes.

quiz.why: The date line is necessary because crossing it means you move forward or backward in time by a day.

wrong.0: While related, the date line is specifically about the calendar date, not just time.
wrong.1: The start of the day is marked by sunrise, not the date line itself.
wrong.3: The equator is a line of latitude, not the date line.

quiz.say: If a city is 15 degrees west of GMT, what is its time?
quiz.why: Moving west means you are behind the reference time, so you subtract one hour.

wrong.0: Students might confuse west with east direction.
wrong.1: Students might forget to calculate the time change.
wrong.2: Students might incorrectly calculate the time difference.
